name: PandaConquest 0.1.0
body:
### Added

- During the alpha, you automatically join the pConquestTest chat channel, shown in your first chat tab, to talk with the team.
- Zoomed out to a continent, the world map shows a capture bar in the middle of each zone with POIs, with the Alliance and Horde badges and each faction's share of the zone's Outposts, Settlements and Hunting Grounds.

### Changed

- The "Connecting to PandaConquest Companion" screen shows a spinning arrow with "Loading".
- The last Guide card, now "A living world", explains why some news can arrive late.
- Hovering the Source / Status column of the POI list explains the status in a tooltip.
- POI list status labels are simpler: Confirmed, Reported, Unconfirmed and Not captured yet.
- "Territory held" counts each place with the faction colour shown in the POI list and on the map, unconfirmed owners included.
- The POI list now shows the same owner color as the map for unconfirmed owners, with "Unconfirmed owner" in the status column.
- The war balance bar shows larger Alliance and Horde crests at its ends, drawn above the crossed swords.
- Capture HUD Horde and Alliance player-count emblems sit in opposite upper corners.
- The minimap button now rides the edge of a square minimap, following PandaUI's Circle or Square setting, and re-places itself when that setting changes.
- Capture HUD player counts now use Horde and Alliance emblems instead of faction names, while the colored POI emblem shows its owner.
- A neutral Settlement can now be captured by one eligible attacker; taking a Settlement from the other faction still requires two.
- Enemy-held Settlement HUDs now show the attacking faction's live player count, such as "Alliance siege: 1/2 attackers inside".
- Settlement sieges now accept unconfirmed linked-objective ownership during testing and launch, preventing sparse P2P confirmation from blocking conquest.
- POI tooltips now label ownership as "Confirmed owner" or "Unconfirmed owner" and omit companion jargon.
- The minimap button now uses a crossed-swords rivalry emblem visually matched to neighboring minimap icons with the stock blue hover; the yellow `Pc` addon icon is unchanged.
- Companion imports advertise the supported import format independently of channel compatibility, allowing cloud ownership to appear as unconfirmed on every account.
- POI names entered in the review interface now appear throughout the PandaConquest windows, map tooltips and capture HUD; compact POI IDs remain the network and storage keys and are used only as a fallback for unnamed places.
- The POI review workflow now returns every validated place without a confirmed name to **To review** and excludes it from the in-game catalog until its name is chosen.

### Fixed

- Minimap POI areas and icons now follow PandaUI's Circle or Square minimap setting, filling square corners when selected.

### Added

- A "PandaConquest" checkbox in the world map header (right of Zoom Out, or left of the maximize button on the minimized map) shows or hides the PandaConquest markers, areas and scout routes on the map; the choice is saved and also applies to the minimap areas.
- Membership tickets: with the companion, your character gets a ticket signed by the PandaConquest cloud and shows it to other players once per session; `/pc ticket` shows who is verified (`/pc ticket bench` times the check). Nobody is blocked for lacking a ticket; only characters banned by an administrator are ignored.
- A chat warning when the game is connected to a server other than OctoWoW: the PandaConquest cloud ignores data from other servers.
- POIs captured while you were offline now show from the cloud, faded: "Claimed by <player>, not verified" when only the capturer reported it, "Unconfirmed (cloud)" once three other players saw it (confirmed as soon as one of them is online), or "Disputed". These never count for gameplay, and every POI stays capturable: a new capture is always numbered above every capture your client knows of, so it wins everywhere.
- `/pc classic` opens the previous text window, kept as a backup of the new design.
- Below level 5, the world map and minimap show no conquest places, and every PandaConquest window tab except the Guide says you must reach level 5 to join the conquest; everything comes back at level 5 without `/reload`.
- The world map shows each Gold Mine, Farm and Forest's current stock (for example `250/320`) under its icon, with a small bar going from green (full) to red (empty).
- POI areas and their icons now also show on the minimap, with the same shapes and faction colors as the world map.
- World map area hover no longer drops over Blizzard's town and landmark markers (for example around Goldshire), nor on spots where the game reports the 3D world under the open map.
- `/pc map hover probe` records where the world map area hover misses and why; `/pc map hover report` summarizes it per area.
- `/pc fileprobe start | report | stop` tests live file exchange through nampower's `CustomData` folder, paired with `tools/file_probe_writer.py`.
- The conquest now requires nampower and a running PandaConquest Companion: without them you get a chat warning, the windows explain what to do and the conquest stays off (like below level 5); it comes back by itself as soon as the companion answers, no `/reload` needed. `/pc companion` shows the connection.
- Companion data can now arrive while you play, a few seconds after the companion starts, instead of only from the file written before the game started.
- New War tab in the PandaConquest window: your scout and army orders, an attack builder (target, units, Assault Capacity, travel time, confirmation), enemy targets with their discovery time and a Scout button, threats to your faction, and a checklist of what each Settlement siege still needs.
- New Guide tab explaining the game loop: gathering, recruitment, capture, garrisons, scouting, attacks and Settlement conquest.
- The Territory tab now shows synchronization health (channel, catch-up, messages waiting, version) and what each data label means.
- A held Settlement shows a larger town icon on the world map and the minimap once it reaches level 2.
- Held Settlements show their level ("Level 1" to "Level 3") under their icon on the world map.

### Changed

- In a Settlement that no faction can besiege yet, neutral or held, players announce their presence once a minute instead of every 10 seconds, which cuts channel traffic there; the fast pace comes back as soon as a siege becomes possible.
- The texts on the HUD progress bar sit slightly higher and use a thin outline instead of a drop shadow.
- At a Gold Mine, Farm or Forest, the HUD now always shows the number of players in the place and the time its stock needs to refill, instead of a single state such as "MAX".

- The capture HUD lines and bar are spaced 7 px apart instead of touching, with 5 px more room above the title and below the last line; the bar is slimmer and the Alliance and Horde badges beside it are larger.
- The capture HUD of Outposts, Settlements and Hunting Grounds now shows the POI's map icon above its name, like resource POIs, in its owner's colors.
- The percents and stock value inside the HUD progress bar use a smaller font.
- The capture HUD sits higher on the screen, and its POI icon no longer touches the title.
- The main window medallion now uses the same panda portrait as the minimap button, without its circular border.
- POI HUD progress bars now animate smoothly, preserve their fill texture instead of squashing it, reach the frame cleanly, and use an even gold border on every edge.
- Capture HUD warnings (for example "not PvP flagged") now show as plain red text at the bottom of the HUD, without the red strip.
- The capture HUD is about 30% smaller with tighter lines, and a -/+ button at its top right collapses it to the progress bar alone; the choice is remembered.
- At a Gold Mine, Farm or Forest, the HUD shows its picture inside a gold ring medallion centered just above the POI name instead of on the top-left corner.
- Resource POIs now use a compact visual HUD: a smaller matching POI picture centered above the corner border, resource-colored stock bars, stock values inside the bar, and icons for gathering state and personal inventory instead of explanatory sentences.
- New PandaConquest window design: a textured Alliance and Horde frame, tabs, panels, bars, unit portraits and icons; the Territory tab shows a war balance bar, the Guide tab one illustrated card per step.
- The capture HUD is textured, without corner crests, with the Alliance share in blue on the left and the Horde share in red on the right; capture alerts and version notices show as red or gold banners.
- Distinct level 1, 2 and 3 Settlement icons on the world map and minimap, round route dots and a new minimap button; the PandaConquest window shows the same POI icons as the map.
- The window's Settlement tab is now the Garrison tab and also opens in Outposts: it shows incoming armies and whether reinforcements are blocked, with the post-battle lock timer, and hides the unit pledge buttons while they are.

- PandaConquest channel messages no longer appear in General or any other chat tab; they show only in a chat tab named exactly `PandaConquest`. The `/pc p2p channelshow` and `channelhide` commands are removed.
- Outpost capture time now depends on its garrison's defense: 3 minutes when empty, up to 20 minutes for a full garrison of the strongest defenders. The time is fixed when the attempt starts, and the HUD and map tooltip show it with the reason.
- Settlements can now be conquered. Your faction must hold every Outpost and Hunting Ground of the zone, the Settlement's garrison must be empty, and an enemy-held Settlement must be scouted first. Then two attackers inside start a 10-minute siege. One attacker left alone freezes the bar, and defenders push it back. A conquest resets the Settlement to level 1, with an empty garrison and War Chest. Holding Settlements raises your Assault Capacity.
- Garrison pledges are now refused from the very start of an enemy capture attempt, not only once its bar has moved.
- Hunting grounds now clearly ask players to enable NamPower in the Octo launcher when it is unavailable.
- Settlement map icons now use the direct 72 × 72 atlas in game: level 1 is one simple building, levels 2 and 3 fill their cells, and every level has matching neutral and Horde/Alliance half- and fully captured states.
- During a capture, the bar state is broadcast every 30 s (instead of every 5 s and at each 5% step); changes (start, contest, capture) stay immediate.
- The addon pauses briefly after a few close messages on the channel, so it no longer triggers the server's anti-spam that silenced the player.
- The addon's name is now spelled "PandaConquest" everywhere (chat messages, version warnings).

### Added

- Attacks: `/pc attack <POI id> <footmen> [riflemen] [mortars]` sends an army from an allied Outpost to an enemy Outpost your faction has scouted (up to 8 Unit Size for now). The units are gone for good; on arrival the battle kills defenders from the garrison and locks unit pledges there for up to 20 minutes. Defenders are warned when an army marches on their place, both sides see the march on the map (only your own faction sees an army's composition), and the battle happens even if the attacker logged off. Unit pledges also close in the last 2 minutes before an enemy army arrives; Settlement upgrade pledges stay open during attacks.

- World map: travelling scouts are drawn as a dotted line from their origin to their target with a moving Knight or Wolf Rider icon, for both factions; a route into a neighboring zone shows its part on each zone.
- Scouting: `/pc scout <POI id>` sends your Knight or Wolf Rider from an allied Outpost to an enemy-held Outpost; on arrival it is discovered for your whole faction for one hour, and its garrison shows in the map tooltip. Both factions see the scout coming. `/pc scout` lists targets and travel times.
- Garrisons: give units from your reserve to an Outpost your faction holds with `/pc pledge <unit> [count] confirm` (`/pc garrison` shows it). A gift can never be taken back; it is refused when the garrison is full (12 Unit Size), during an enemy capture, or for Scouts, and a capture empties the garrison. The window's new Settlement tab, enabled when you stand in a Settlement, shows its garrison, level and gold/wood War Chest; Settlements cannot be held yet, so their pledges stay closed.
- PandaConquest window: click the PandaConquest button on the minimap edge (drag it to move it; its place is saved) or type `/pc` (or `/pc ui`) to open it. Its Resources tab shows your gold, wood and food and the resource stocks, its Army tab shows your reserve with +1/+5 recruit buttons and why a recruitment is refused, and its Territory tab shows who holds each Outpost and Hunting Grounds, marking reports from other players as unverified and unconfirmed. `/pc help` now lists the commands.
- Units and recruitment: inside an Outpost held by your faction, `/pc recruit <unit> [count]` recruits Footman/Grunt, Rifleman/Headhunter, Mortar Team/Demolisher or the Knight/Wolf Rider scout, paid at once in gold, wood and food; `/pc army` shows your personal reserve (up to 25 Unit Size), the costs and why a recruitment is refused.
- Gathering: in a gold mine, a forest or a farm, you automatically gather gold, wood or food (5 every 10 s, same conditions as capture). Each place has a stock shared by both factions, which runs out then regenerates; it shows on the map and in the HUD, and `/pc res` shows your resources.
- At login, the owners of POIs captured while you were away are caught up from other players: shown "unconfirmed" (faded color) until several players agree.
- Below level 5, the server forbids talking on channels: you no longer take part in POI capture (Outposts and hunting grounds) and the HUD says so; you take part again from level 5.

### Fixed

- Installing ClassicAPI no longer causes a login error while PandaConquest replaces an invalid membership ticket.
- Membership-ticket verification no longer errors while idle on clients without Lua coroutines.
- After a `/reload` inside a captured Outpost or Hunting Ground, the capture HUD no longer shows it as neutral with an empty bar.
- A thin blue and brown line no longer shows under the top border of the capture HUD.
- Turning PvP off with `/pvp` inside a POI now stops capturing and gathering at once and the HUD says "PvP toggled off", instead of counting you until the five-minute PvP flag runs out.
- POI HUD borders now use one continuous frame, with clean corner and rail joins.
- The PandaConquest title keeps its full upper outline instead of looking cropped.
- The HUD capture bar shows the factions' progress again instead of staying grey.
- At a POI your faction already holds and nobody is taking, the HUD no longer shows a capture objective (Hunting Grounds "Kill the required creatures", Outpost capture time); at Hunting Grounds it asks you to defend when the enemy is taking it, and to capture it otherwise.

### Security

- An owner announced by a single player, with no observed capture, can no longer settle on the map for good or block later captures.

Channel compatibility level: `PC5`. Versions at `PC4` or earlier no longer share their captures with this one: every player must update.
